claims.text: Money is anything that people generally accept as payment for goods and services and for settling debts; its forms include coins, notes and bank deposits.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: The functions of money are the jobs it does in exchange: a medium of exchange that passes from buyer to seller and so removes the double coincidence of wants that barter needs, a unit of account that measures value in one common unit, and a store of value that keeps worth from one period to the next.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: The characteristics of money are the qualities a thing needs before people accept it as money: acceptability, durability, portability, divisibility, uniformity and scarcity.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: Characteristics of money and functions of money are different lists: the functions are what money does in an exchange, whereas the characteristics are what money has to be to do those jobs; the test is to ask whether an answer names a job performed (a function) or a quality carried (a characteristic).

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: A commercial bank is a financial institution that accepts deposits from households and firms, lends the pooled funds to borrowers, and moves payments between accounts.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: A central bank is the institution that issues the country's notes and coins, holds the government's account and settles its payments, keeps the deposits of the commercial banks, and stands behind them when deposits are withdrawn in a rush; it serves the government and the banking system rather than private customers.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: Banks matter to each group because commercial banks pool many small deposits into larger loans: producers borrow to bridge the gap between paying costs and receiving revenue and to buy equipment, consumers keep savings safe and pay at a distance, and the government pays salaries and collects taxes through the banking system.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.
